Paul uses it as counterpoint to ἐκδημέω ('be away from home'), creating a spatial metaphor for the believer's dual location: at home in the body but away from the Lord, or away from the body and at home with the Lord. The verb establishes embodied life as temporary residence, with true home elsewhere."

The Spanish (estando-en-casa, estar-en-casa) and French (être-chez-soi) literalize the at-home language,...
